"I'm worried you'll become my blind spot," Il-hyun murmured, his baritone dropping. "If things get messy, the Chairman won't hesitate to take you hostage just to put a leash on my throat."

"I'm Lee Ja-kyeong."

He lifted his chin with unvarnished arrogance. Watching the display, Il-hyun burst into a genuine laugh. To the rest of the world, the boy was a lethal, ice-cold phantom; to Il-hyun, he looked like an indignant stray kitten baring tiny claws at a black panther.

Catching the patronizing amusement, Jakyeong scowled. "Don't laugh. It's irritating."

"Humor me, then. Just take a month off."

Jakyeong turned the idea over in his head. A whole month abroad... That's more than enough time to vanish into thin air.

As his eyes darted with quiet calculations, Il-hyun cut through the thought with razor-sharp timing:

"Try running away, and I won't bother with a helicopter this time. I'll scramble fighter jets."

Instead of resting in bed, Wang Ryun was brawling in the middle of the concourse. He shoved past the private security details trying to restrain him, while nurses hovered at the edges, wringing their hands in panic.

"Get your hands off me! I don't need your damn treatment! I'm leaving!"

Han let out a weary sigh. When Ryun lost his temper, he turned into an unstoppable freight train. His hospital gown was already soaked through with fresh crimson where his surgical sutures had torn open.

Holding the elevator door, Han turned to Jakyeong. "Want me to handle him?"

Jakyeong clicked his tongue.

Han was far too soft-hearted for this. Without wasting a breath, Jakyeong broke into a dead sprint down the hall.

"Ryun!"

Hearing the shout, the raging giant wheeled around.

In one blinding, fluid leap, Jakyeong kicked off the corridor wall to gain leverage, whipping his leg around in a blistering spinning heel kick.

CRACK.

The heel connected flush with the point of Ryun’s jaw, snapping his head sideways as his eyes rolled straight into his skull.

With a heavy, concussive thud, Wang Ryun’s massive frame collapsed flat across the linoleum, out cold.
